That the word of Jesus did not fall along the path or among the thorns, insofar as it depends on us, we will boast in the Lord. For we have understood what was said; that is why the evil one did not snatch away what was sown in our heart. And that it was not sown among the thorns either, many will bear us witness, seeing that neither the cares of this age, nor the deceitfulness of riches, nor the pleasures of life have been able to hinder the word of God in our souls. It remains for people to be in doubt whether, as far as we are concerned, the word of God fell on rocky ground or on good soil. For affliction and persecution have arisen because of the word, and a time of great temptation has come, when the one sown on rocky ground is exposed, along with those who did not go deep and did not receive Jesus into the depths of their soul; but the one who understands the word bears fruit and holds fast the word to the end, yielding a hundredfold in endurance.

For we hear how Scripture presents those who, after seeming to have received the holy teachings with joy, stumble in a time of affliction or persecution, and who stumble because they have no root but believe for a time. According to Matthew it says: "As for the one sown on rocky ground, this is the one who hears the word and immediately receives it with joy; yet he has no root in himself but lasts only for a while, and when affliction or persecution arises because of the word, he immediately stumbles." According to Mark: "These are the ones sown on rocky ground, who, when they hear the word, immediately receive it with joy; and they have no root in themselves but last only for a while; then, when affliction or persecution arises because of the word, they immediately stumble." According to Luke: "And those on the rock are the ones who, when they hear, receive the word with joy; and these have no root; they believe for a while, and in a time of temptation they fall away." But teaching about those who bear fruit well, it says: "As for the one sown on the good soil, this is the one who hears the word and understands it, who indeed bears fruit and yields, one a hundredfold, another sixty, another thirty"; or: "And those are the ones sown on the good soil, who hear the word and accept it and bear fruit, thirtyfold and sixtyfold and a hundredfold"; or: "And as for that in the good soil, these are the ones who, having heard the word with a noble and good heart, hold it fast and bear fruit with endurance."

According to the apostle, then, since "you are God's field, God's building"—a field in the good soil and a building on the rock—let us stand unshaken against the storm as God's building, and as God's field let us pay no heed to the evil one, nor to the affliction or persecution that arise because of the word, nor to the cares of this age, nor to the deceitfulness of riches, nor to the pleasures of life. Rather, despising all these things, let us take up the carefree spirit of wisdom, hasten toward the riches that have no deceit in them at all, and press on toward the—if I may call them so—pleasures of the paradise of delight, reckoning in each of our hardships that "our momentary light affliction is producing for us an eternal weight of glory beyond all measure," as we look not to the things that are seen but to the things that are not seen.

Let us also recognize that what was said about Abel, who was slain by the murderous and unjust Cain, applies to all whose blood has been unjustly shed. For let us consider that the words "The voice of your brother's blood cries out to me from the ground" are spoken also about each of the martyrs, the voice of whose blood cries out to God from the ground.

And perhaps, just as we were bought with the precious blood of Jesus, after Jesus received the name that is above every name, so some will be bought with the precious blood of the martyrs, while the martyrs themselves are exalted more highly than they would have been had they become righteous but not borne witness unto death. For there is good reason why death in martyrdom is properly called exaltation, as is clear from the words "If I am lifted up from the earth, I will draw all people to myself." Let us too, then, glorify God by exalting him through our own death, since the one who bears witness will glorify God by his own death. This too we have learned from John, who said: "He said this to indicate by what kind of death he would glorify God."

These things I have dictated to you as well as I could and as far as I was able, and I pray that they may prove useful to you for the present contest. But if you, now above all, as people worthy to see more of the mysteries of God, grasp greater and richer things, more effective for the task before you, and so despise these things as childish and trivial, I too would pray that this may be so for you. For what matters to you is not that your affairs be brought to completion through us, but that they be brought to completion by any means at all. And may they indeed be brought to completion through words more divine and wiser, surpassing all human nature, and through the wisdom of God.
